answer: Agents selling raven counts from an orchard near a wharf earn API credits through deposit aging. Each locked coin accrues one credit per day; withdrawals stop accrual, and spending atomically consumes credits. New accounts receive no free allowance. Moving a deposit cannot copy its accrued credits, and splitting it among aliases preserves total coin-days. A swarm must tie up capital for time to gain access, rather than merely create names. This limits cheap sybils, not wealthy operators.
